name: I've Managed Fine — Six Objections, Six Films

sequence.note: Cost Is Not The Reason answers one objection loudly. This campaign answers six objections quietly, to a different reader: an established owner, usually older, who has run a good business for years without a website and does not believe they need one. Same SKU (FAM-FOOT-199), different register. It is not a sequel and does not depend on that campaign having been seen.

business_goal: Reach established, profitable, web-absent business owners who are not postponing out of cost but out of a reasonable read of decades of their own evidence. Answer the six objections they actually voice, one film each, without condescension — and give the owner a set of films short enough to send to one prospect at a time.

primary_offer.scope: One focused landing-page website, one year of FAMtastic-managed hosting, and first-year domain registration when needed — or connection of a domain the customer already owns. Business email (FAM-BUSINESS-EMAIL) and maintenance (FAM-MAINTENANCE) are separate products and are never implied to be included.

audience.label: Owners who have run a real business for years with no website
audience.profile: Real customers, real revenue, no web presence. Typically older. Expert in their trade, beginner on anything web. Frequently burned once by a 'computer guy'.
audience.why_they_have_not: Not laziness and not ignorance. They are pattern-matching on decades of evidence that word of mouth worked — because it did.
audience.tone_contract: Never mock the objection. Never imply they are behind. The words 'still', 'finally' and 'even you' are banned from every asset in this campaign. Respect is the whole tone.

creative_thesis: Each film states one objection in the owner's own words, in quotation marks, concedes what is true about it out loud, and only then answers with a mechanism. No statistic, no urgency, no named competitor. The images are photographs of objects this viewer has touched — an empty sign bracket, a card-file drawer, a cash drawer, a brass letter slot — on warm paper, never neon.

films.objection: I've managed fine for thirty years.
films.answer: True, and the customers who found you did it differently each decade.

films.objection: My customers know where I am.
films.answer: The ones you have, yes. The question is the ones who moved in last year.
You will not touch it. Neither does anyone else who has one.

films.objection: I tried before and got burned.
films.answer: Name the real pattern: paid up front, no proof, then silence. We run it the other way around.
55 cents a day. One page, one year of hosting, a domain that is yours — and what renews, said before it is asked.
Then it matters more, not less. A buyer buys what transfers, and a domain transfers.

direct_send.note: Every film is built to stand alone with no campaign context, because the owner sends them one-to-one. Which film answers which objection is in SEND-DIRECT.md.

channels.exclusion_reason: Owner-blocked as of 2026-09-05: YouTube's OAuth token is expired and TikTok is not approved for public posting. X and LinkedIn are out of scope for this campaign. Queueing to a broken channel manufactures a failure; these six drops target only the two channels that publish today.

spend.breakdown: No provider call of any kind. Plates were already on disk (generated for the platform-dependency drop before this campaign existed). Narration is local Voicebox/kokoro on Apple Silicon — free, no API key, no metered credits. Grading, rendering and muxing are local ffmpeg and Chrome. HyperFrames renders locally; its paid hosted cloud path was not used.

claims_policy.statistics: none used — every argument is a mechanism, per BRAND.md
claims_policy.delivery_time: no delivery-time promise appears anywhere; the '48 hours' claim live on older posts is not repeated
claims_policy.renewal_disclosure: every film that names $199 also states '$9.99 a month, plus the domain' on screen
claims_policy.reviewer_disclosure: the proof-first film states that a person reviews the designs before the customer sees them
